name: Marlow Foods (Quorn)
note: The incumbent. A 2015 report gave about 38,000 tonnes of projected mycoprotein capacity after a third fermenter.

name: Meati
note: Raised $450M+, entered an assignment for creditors in spring 2025, assets sold for $4M. The new owner stopped production in November 2025; in December 2025 the county seized the plant's equipment for unpaid taxes, and an online auction followed in spring 2026. The core fermentation assets did not sell at auction. In September 2026 Ayana Bio and Zenfold Sustainable Technologies bought twelve 25,000 liter tanks with their seed trains, 300,000 liters in all, for $75,000, to ship to India for plant cell culture.

name: Mycorena
note: Bankrupt July 2024. Naplasol, of the VEOS group, bought it in August 2024 and moved production of its Promyc ingredient to Bree in Belgium.

name: Nature's Fynd
note: Fungal protein grown on liquid surfaces.

name: Prime Roots
note: Mycelium based deli meats.

name: Infinite Roots (formerly Mushlabs)
note: Germany. Mycelium grown on food industry side streams. Bought Bosque Foods, a German maker of whole cut mycelium meat, in May 2026.

name: Enifer
note: Mycoprotein from industrial side streams, Finland.

name: The Protein Brewery
note: Fermotein, the first mycelium protein cleared as a novel food in the EU, June 2026.

name: BMC Ingredients (formerly Better Meat Co)
note: United States. California maker of Rhiza, a mycoprotein ingredient. Closed a 31 million dollar Series A in 2025, one of the few large fermentation rounds that year. Health Canada cleared Rhiza in July 2026, and India's food regulator approved it in October 2026, its fourth market after the United States, Singapore and Canada. Sales in India are planned from the second quarter of 2027.

name: Hedgehog
note: Palo Alto, about $12.8M raised (Specter).

name: Libre Foods
note: In June 2025 Planetary bought Libre Foods' core brand, commercial agreements and intellectual property. Terms were not disclosed.

name: Fushine and More Meat (China)
note: Fushine runs a 1,200 ton mycoprotein line and won China's first mycoprotein approval; More Meat is building a 20,000 ton plant, the fastest capacity growth outside Europe.

name: Michroma
note: Fungal red colorant, won the first prize of 250,000 euros.

name: Chromologics
note: Natural colors made by fungal fermentation, about $14.7M raised.

name: Mycolever
note: Fungal bioingredients for cosmetics.

name: M2 Ingredients
note: Organic mushroom ingredient maker; its chief science officer co-chairs the AOAC Functional Mushrooms Initiative working group, which started with lion's mane in 2025.

name: Applied Food Sciences
note: MycoThrive branded mushroom ingredient.

name: Maypro
note: Ingredient supplier that distributes NuCelium in its mushroom line.

name: GrapeKing Bio
note: Lion's mane mycelium standardized to erinacine A.

name: DIRTEA and RYZE
note: Direct to consumer mushroom drinks and powders.

name: MycoWorks
note: Announced the closure of its South Carolina plant in October 2025 and shifted from growing mycelium to sourcing and finishing it. Acquired by DFX Corp in February 2026.

name: Bolt Threads, Mylo
note: Mylo mycelium leather paused in 2023 after funding ran out near commercial scale.

name: Ecovative and MyForest Foods
note: Mycelium platform licensing into packaging and food.

name: Visibuilt
note: Fungal replacement for bitumen.

name: Hexagon Bio
note: Mines fungal genomes for new molecules; now focused on payloads for antibody drug conjugates, with a Corteva joint venture for crop protection from December 2025. Raised a 62 million dollar Series C led by The Column Group in October 2026, to start a Phase 1 trial of its lead drug in the first half of 2027.

name: Antheia
note: United States, Menlo Park. Engineers yeast to make plant derived drug ingredients, such as the starting materials for pain and overdose medicines, instead of growing and extracting plants. Completed its Series C in January 2026 and plans United States manufacturing.

name: Novogaia
note: Machine learning on fungal natural products.

name: Biohm
note: Microbiome products that target fungi, about $13M raised.

name: MycoMine
note: Sweden. Uses fungi to recover metals from mine waste. A Vinnova funded study it led, May 2023 to May 2024, reported 93 percent copper recovery and 80 to 90 percent for lead, zinc and arsenic, according to the funder's project page.

name: Novobiom
note: Fungi for cleaning polluted soil.

name: HIRO Technologies
note: Fungi that break down used diapers.

name: Rhizocore
note: Mycorrhizal fungi for tree planting, about $5.2M raised.

name: Quorum Earth
note: United States. Brooklyn maker of a biopesticide from the fungus Metarhizium against varroa mites, to protect honeybees.

name: Sylvan
note: The largest spawn maker. KKR remains its majority owner; Novo Holdings made a direct investment in April 2025.

name: Far West Fungi
note: California grower and retailer.

name: Genome mining
note: Hexagon Bio and Novogaia show it can attract pharma and agriculture partners.

name: Solid Fermentation Innovation
note: Development and pilot scale up for fungi grown on solid material, 10 to 350 kg, Israel. Publishes an open knowledge base of 216 fermentation conditions with GFI Israel.

name: Testing standards
note: AOAC Functional Mushrooms Initiative, launched 2025 under its botanical integrity program, with M2 Ingredients and Fungi Perfecti on the working group.

name: Fungal electronics research
note: Jens Laurids Sorensen, science award for a fungal battery.

name: Zhonggu Junchuang
note: China. Grows mycelium only, selling mycelium flour, powders, purees, snacks, beverages and mycelium coffee. Building a hub in western China with about 150 million yuan of government backing. Dao Foods invested in 2024.

name: CellX (brand Mourish)
note: China and United States. Ferments morel mycelium into high protein jerky snacks. Formerly a cultivated meat company. About 20 million dollars raised to date.

name: Fujian Wanchen Food Group (formerly Wanchen Biotechnology)
note: China. One of the country's dominant factory cultivation enterprises for edible mushrooms. Renamed from Fujian Wanchen Biotechnology Group in January 2026.

name: Guangdong Dongyangguang Pharmaceutical
note: China. Factory cultivation of Ophiocordyceps sinensis biomass for food and supplement use across seven production bases.

name: Agroludens
note: Japan. Grows koji mold on rice protein to make CoMeat mycoprotein, sold through its own shop.

name: NoMy Japan
note: Japan. Grows a filamentous fungus on by-products of sugar manufacturing to make protein, in Sapporo. Subsidiary of Norwegian Mycelium.

name: Norwegian Mycelium (NoMy)
note: Norway. Ferments mycelium on food and agricultural by-products into mycoprotein. Parent of NoMy Japan.

name: Dhampur Bio Organics
note: India. Sugar producer that signed an exclusive license from Planetary on October 19, 2026 to make mycoprotein in India from its own sugar and molasses, disclosed in a filing to the Indian stock exchanges. The first term is ten years and Dhampur pays Planetary a 10 percent royalty. The filing names no start date, site or capacity.

name: Zero Cow Factory
note: India. Yeast precision fermentation of animal free casein and whey from Surat, starting with A2 beta casein. Raised 4 million dollars in 2023.

name: Emmay
note: Vietnam. Ho Chi Minh City startup making mycoprotein foods from shiitake mycelium, including pate and pork floss analogues.

name: Mush Foods
note: Israel. Blends mycelium with shiitake and king oyster into 50Cut, a mix chefs use to replace half the meat in a dish. Raised 6.2 million dollars.

name: Typcal
note: Brazil. Ferments a fungal strain on brewery, bakery, dairy and starch side streams into fresh and powdered mycoprotein. Opened a new facility in December 2025.

name: ENOUGH (formerly 3F Bio)
note: United Kingdom, with its plant at Sas van Gent in the Netherlands. Biomass fermentation of Fusarium venenatum into ABUNDA mycoprotein. About 103 million dollars raised in total.

name: Nosh.bio
note: Germany. Ferments fungal biomass into Koji Chunks, a single ingredient meat alternative launched with the Zur Muhlen Group.

name: Kynda
note: Germany. Ferments mycelium on soy, oat and rice pulp side streams into mycoprotein meat. About 5.8 million euros raised in total.

name: Matr Foods
note: Denmark. Ferments mycelium on upcycled beetroot, potato, lupin, pea and oat into mince and burgers. Raised 40 million euros including European Investment Bank debt.

name: Millow
note: Sweden. Dry fermentation grows filamentous mycelium on oats into a two ingredient mycoprotein. About 3.4 million dollars from EU grants.

name: Planetary
note: Switzerland. Ferments Fusarium venenatum into mycoprotein at a plant next to a sugar mill in Aarberg, selling to Aldi Suisse. Licensing its process to Dhampur in India.

name: Revo Foods
note: Austria. Structures mycoprotein by 3D printing into whole cut salmon analogues, sold in over 20 European countries.

name: MycoVibes Biotech
note: Poland. Ferments shiitake mycelium into wet biomass, concentrates and blends as a mycoprotein ingredient. Took a 300,000 euro research grant in 2025.

name: Amano Enzyme
note: Japan. Specialty enzymes made by culturing microorganisms, including an AMP deaminase produced by the mold Aspergillus melleus. Nagoya.

name: Dyadic International
note: United States. Built a protein production platform on the filamentous fungus Thermothelomyces heterothallica. In July 2025 it began to do business as Dyadic Applied BioSolutions and moved toward proteins for uses other than drugs and vaccines.

name: MycoTechnology
note: United States. Ferments mushroom mycelium into a bitter blocker and a fermented plant protein. Raised 85 million dollars in 2022 from an Oman Investment Authority affiliate, more than 220 million in total.

name: Chinova Bioworks
note: Canada. Extracts chitosan fibre from white button mushrooms and sells it as a natural preservative for food and drink. Filed with Food Standards Australia New Zealand in 2024.

name: Octarine Bio
note: Denmark. Engineered baker's yeast making color pigments. Earlier work put Psilocybe cubensis genes into yeast to make psilocybin. Series A reached 12.8 million euros in January 2026.

name: Four Sigmatic
note: United States, built on a Finnish mushroom coffee tradition. Mushroom coffee, creamers and instant teas with lion's mane and other extracts, in more than 6,200 stores.

name: Zhejiang Shouxiangu Pharmaceutical
note: China. Ganoderma lucidum spore powder and extract alongside Dendrobium and other traditional medicine products. Listed in Shanghai as 603896.

name: GanoHerb Technology (Fujian Xianzhilou)
note: China. Cultivates and extracts Ganoderma lucidum and sells the processed ingredient into supplements and functional foods.

name: Biosan Biotech
note: China. Contract manufacturer of organic mushroom powders and extracts across reishi, lion's mane, chaga, maitake, shiitake, turkey tail, tremella and cordyceps. Lishui.

name: Greenyn Biotechnology
note: Taiwan. Grows Antrodia cinnamomea mycelium by solid state fermentation and sells it as an ingredient. Holds a United States new dietary ingredient number.

name: Vigor Young
note: Taiwan. Antrodia cinnamomea capsules from fruiting body and mycelium powder. Its raw material passed a safety test by Taiwan's food and drug agency.

name: Amino Up
note: Japan. Makes a standardized extract of cultured shiitake mycelia sold as an immune supplement and used in clinical trials. Sapporo.

name: Nammex
note: Supplies certified organic whole mushroom extract powders in reishi, lion's mane, chaga, cordyceps and turkey tail to supplement and food brands, grown at partner sites in China.

name: Shroomwell (Chaga OU)
note: Estonia. Grows and extracts medicinal mushrooms for supplements and inoculates tree seedlings for forestry. Planning a facility of up to 50 million euros beside a pulp mill at Kunda.

name: Hifas da Terra
note: Spain. Mushroom based supplements with its own labs and production in Galicia. Entered the United States market in April 2026.

name: Life Cykel
note: Australia, with a manufacturing arm in Wisconsin. Liquid functional mushroom extracts in lion's mane, reishi, cordyceps and chaga.

name: SCYNEXIS
note: United States. Develops a triterpenoid antifungal class derived from enfumafungin. Its approved drug is licensed to GSK, which paid 90 million dollars upfront in 2023 plus milestones.

name: F2G
note: United Kingdom. Develops olorofim, the first drug in a new antifungal class, for invasive aspergillosis. Raised 100 million dollars in September 2024 led by the AMR Action Fund.

name: Basilea Pharmaceutica
note: Switzerland. Antifungal and antibacterial company that bought the broad spectrum antifungal candidate fosmanogepix from Pfizer in November 2023 for 37 million dollars upfront.

name: Amplyx Pharmaceuticals
note: United States. Developed fosmanogepix for invasive fungal infections. Acquired by Pfizer in April 2021, which then sold the drug's rights to Basilea in November 2023.

name: Mycovia Pharmaceuticals
note: United States. Makes an oral azole antifungal for recurrent vaginal thrush, the first medication approved for that indication.

name: Kaken Pharmaceutical
note: Japan. Developed and sells a topical triazole antifungal for fungal nail infection, licensed outside Japan.

name: LifeMine Therapeutics
note: United States. Mines fungal genomes for small molecules against chosen drug targets, then retrieves them with synthetic biology. Raised 175 million dollars in 2022, more than 295 million in total.

name: Golden Biotechnology
note: Taiwan. Develops a purified compound from the Taiwanese fungus Antrodia camphorata and sells a freeze dried mycelium ingredient.

name: BIOHM Health
note: United States. Probiotic and gut testing products built on the idea that gut health depends on fungal as well as bacterial balance. Its cofounder coined the term mycobiome.

name: Psyence Biomedical
note: Canada, Nasdaq listed, trials in Australia. Nature derived psilocybin medicine, lead candidate in a mid stage trial in palliative cancer care. First patient dosed April 2026.

name: Optimi Health
note: Canada. Licensed manufacturer of pharmaceutical grade botanical psilocybin from its own mushroom facilities in British Columbia, supplying clinical programs in Australia and Canada.

name: Filament Health
note: Canada. Botanical psilocybin drug candidates supplied to clinical trials. Delisted from Cboe Canada in May 2025 and moved to the OTCQB market. Red Light Holland completed its purchase of the company on April 29, 2026.

name: Red Light Holland
note: Canada. Grows and sells psilocybin truffles in the Netherlands through a subsidiary, supplying more than 125 retail stores. Quarterly revenue fell about 45 percent year on year to September 2025.

name: Mindset Pharma
note: Canada. Designed improved psilocybin analogues for treatment resistant depression. Otsuka agreed to buy it in September 2023 for about 80 million Canadian dollars in cash.

name: Reunion Neuroscience
note: Canada. A psilocin analogue prodrug for postnatal depression, spun out of Field Trip's research arm. Taken private by MPM BioImpact in August 2023, then raised 103 million dollars in May 2024.

name: Field Trip Health and Wellness
note: Canada. Ran psychedelic therapy clinics and a Jamaican psilocybin cultivation and research laboratory. Obtained creditor protection in March 2023 and sold the Jamaican laboratory for 350,000 dollars that May. Close to 100 million Canadian dollars was spent over its life.

name: Core One Labs
note: Canada. Developed biosynthetic psilocybin by fermentation rather than growing mushrooms. In default from February 2024, trading suspended that August, the whole board and management resigned in May 2025, and it was delisted in September 2025.

name: Wesana Health Holdings
note: Canada. Developed a psilocybin and cannabidiol combination for major depressive disorder. Shareholders approved the sale of the psychedelics assets in June 2023 and the company now has no operating business.

name: Mydecine Innovations Group
note: Canada. Developed second generation psilocybin analogues for post traumatic stress and nicotine addiction. Held 234 dollars of cash at 30 June 2025 against a working capital deficit of 15.3 million, with no research spending in that half year and a management cease trade order from May 2025, which bars its chief executive and chief financial officer from trading its shares.

name: HAVN Life Sciences
note: Canada. Grew psilocybin mushrooms in Jamaica for export and testing and sold natural health products. First harvest in August 2021, restructuring by September 2022, listing suspended in November 2023 with cease trade orders in two provinces.

name: MYCEL
note: South Korea. Hyundai Motor spin out growing pure mycelium into leather sheets for clothing, bags, shoes and car interiors, plus a fungal protein food. Raised 10 million dollars pre Series A in 2022.

name: Earthform
note: South Korea. Grows mycelium on farm and fishery byproducts into moulded cushion packaging that replaces polystyrene foam. Seed round closed in January 2025.

name: Mycotech Lab (MYCL)
note: Indonesia. Mylea mycelium leather, BIOBO binderless mycelium board and furniture from farm and timber waste. Reported sales contracts of 10 million dollars with Under Armour, Decathlon and Camper.

name: MYCL Japan
note: Japan. Licensed offshoot of Mycotech Lab in Nagano growing mushroom leather and pressing leftover substrate into boards.

name: Dharaksha Ecosolutions
note: India. Grows paddy straw with mycelium into moulded packaging, developing bonded boards and films. Raised 24.8 crore rupees in 2024.

name: Roha Biotech
note: India. Grows mycelium with banana fibre, sugarcane husk, coir and corn waste into compostable moulded packaging at about four tons a month near Chennai.

name: MycoTile
note: Kenya. Grows mycelium on farm residue into wall, roof and insulation panels for low cost housing, with facilities from the Kenya Industrial Research and Development Institute.

name: MycoHAB
note: Namibia. Grows oyster mushrooms on invasive encroacher bush, then presses the spent substrate into structural mycelium blocks for housing. Works with MIT and the Shack Dwellers Federation of Namibia.

name: MycoSphere
note: United Arab Emirates. Grows date palm waste with mycelium into acoustic panels, wall and ceiling cladding and architectural relief, from Al Quoz in Dubai.

name: MadeRight
note: Israel. Ferments fungi on industrial organic waste and extracts additive pellets for bioplastic packaging. Raised 2 million dollars in 2023.

name: Spora
note: Chile. Grows mycelium from wild Patagonian and Amazonian fungi into substitutes for leather, wool and wood. Launched a luxury collection in 2026 with Harrods and The Peninsula Hotels named.

name: Mush
note: Brazil. Parana state company growing mycelium on farm waste into packaging, furniture and decor. Likely related to Muush, a leather alternative maker in the same city. Raised 900,000 reais from Irani Ventures in 2023.

name: Mosh
note: Argentina. Grows local farm waste with mycelium into home compostable moulded packaging for cosmetics, wine and fashion brands.

name: Mycorium Biotech
note: Argentina. Upcycles agro industrial waste into mycelium leather for handbags and accessories, aiming at footwear and car trim. Rosario, founded 2022.

name: M-Based
note: Turkey. Develops FOMES, a mushroom based leather substitute, from Ankara. Raised about 700,000 dollars seed in October 2026.

name: Myceen
note: Estonia. Grows mycelium with forestry and farm waste into building insulation, acoustic panels and lamps. Over 2 million euros in grants by August 2024.

name: Biomyc
note: Bulgaria. Mycelium composite packaging including a standardised line. Clients listed include Mercedes-Benz, KIA, Treasury Wine Estates and BAT. Formerly named Shift Ideas.

name: Myco
note: Czechia. Grows mycelium on sawdust, waste paper, textiles and hemp into packaging replacing polystyrene, plus scent carrier parts. Collaborations named with Skoda and Meopta.

name: Grown.bio (formerly Krown Design)
note: Netherlands. Grows mycelium on Dutch farm waste into moulded packaging, insulation panels and interior objects. Launched as Krown Design at Dutch Design Week in 2016. The rename matters for anyone searching the old name.

name: NEFFA (MycoTEX)
note: Netherlands. Grows mycelium into seamless made to measure garments and textile sheets, moulded without cutting or sewing.

name: Loop Biotech
note: Netherlands. Grows hemp fibre inoculated with mycelium into the Living Cocoon, a biodegradable coffin, plus urns. Over 2,500 burials and capacity of 500 coffins a month as of October 2025.

name: PermaFungi
note: Belgium. Grows mycelium on Brussels sawdust and wood waste into packaging, shipping fillers, lamps and wall tiles.

name: Ecoroots
note: Ireland. Grows mycelium on brewery and distillery spent grain, hemp and sawdust into moulded packaging, from a 750 square meter site in Cork.

name: Magical Mushroom Company
note: United Kingdom. Moulds mycelium with recycled biowaste into protective packaging at plants in Nottinghamshire.

name: Mykor
note: United Kingdom, with a pilot factory in Portugal. Binds biomass residues with mycelium into rigid and loose fill building insulation.

name: Mogu (SQIM)
note: Italy. Pure mycelium acoustic panels, flooring and surface finishes, plus Ephea leather. Raised 11 million euros in January 2024 with Kering Ventures participating. Balenciaga showed an Ephea coat in its autumn winter 2022 collection.

name: Grado Zero Espace
note: Italy. Makes Muskin, a suede like material cut from the cap of Phellinus ellipsoideus. Reported acquired by Pangaia in 2021. Whether Muskin is still produced is not stated in the source.

name: Mushroom Material
note: New Zealand, registered in Singapore. Mycelium bound pellets from farm waste that mould into polystyrene replacement packaging and insulation. Funding reported as 8.5 million dollars in 2024 and about 5.5 million in 2025, a conflict to resolve before quoting either.

name: Fungi Solutions
note: Australia. Melbourne company growing mycelium through landfill bound waste including textiles, sawdust, grape marc and cigarette butts, and making custom packaging, fungal leather, sculpture, signage and lighting.

name: Shanghai Xuerong Bio-Technology
note: China. Industrial grower of enoki, shimeji, king oyster, seafood mushroom, button and shiitake. Listed in Shenzhen as 300511.

name: Tianshui Zhongxing Bio-technology
note: China. Listed grower of enoki, king oyster and beech mushrooms. Also converts fungal crop waste into high protein food. Leased a new edible fungi factory in December 2025.

name: Jiangsu Hualv Biological Technology
note: China. Grower of enoki, white jade and crab flavored shimeji and maitake, with about 2,500 staff at Suqian. Listed as 300970. Its English name is Jiangsu Chinagreen Biological Technology.

name: Chongqing Hualv Biotechnology
note: China. Enoki factory producing 50,000 tons a year at a base in Lushui village described as the largest in southwest China. First phase investment of 420 million yuan.

name: Jiangsu Ruyiqing Mushroom Biotechnology
note: China. Construction began in 2018 on a bottle cultivation plant at Lianyungang planned for 700,000 bottles a day.

name: Fujian Vanchen Mushroom Biotechnology
note: China. Factory grower of enoki, brown shimeji and white beech at 110 tons a day.

name: Sichuan Qiying Mushroom
note: China. King oyster mushrooms and Cordyceps militaris in Pengxi County, about 200 tons a day combined.

name: Chengdu Huiguyuan Biotechnology
note: China. Planned 60 tons a day of Hypsizygus marmoreus and 20 tons a day of yellow enoki, with launch set for April 2018. No newer status found.

name: Shanxi Tianjilong Biotechnology
note: China. Automated bottle grown Pleurotus nebrodensis at Shangluo, more than 4,000 tons of fresh mushrooms a year.

name: Shandong Qihe Biotechnology
note: China. Produces 150 to 200 million shiitake spawn logs a year and sells spawn and fresh mushrooms worldwide. Opened production in Poland in 2020; a site in Spain was under construction in 2023.

name: Exotic Mushroom Center
note: Poland. Subsidiary of Shandong Qihe growing shiitake and king oyster at Krzekotow and supplying substrate logs to nearby farms.

name: HOKTO
note: Japan. The country's largest mushroom company. Grows bunashimeji, eryngii and maitake and also makes cultivation materials and packaging. Operates a factory in Malaysia.

name: Yukiguni Factory (formerly Yukiguni Maitake)
note: Japan. Maitake, king trumpet and beech mushrooms, founded 1983 at Minami Uonuma. Taken private by Bain Capital in 2015, which sold 49 percent to Shinmei in 2017. Now listed again on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market under code 1375, and renamed Yukiguni Factory on 1 April 2025. Revenue of 53.1 billion yen in the year to March 2025. Has announced entry into the Netherlands and plans for mushroom based meat substitutes.

name: Daemyung Farms
note: South Korea. Year round bottle cultivation enoki grower with about 5,000 tons of capacity, exporting roughly 50 tons a month.

name: Thanh Cao Kinoko
note: Vietnam. Enoki and oyster mushrooms at 1.5 tons a day on a 3,000 square meter site near Hanoi. Reported investment of 3 million dollars.

name: Long Khanh Kinoko
note: Vietnam. Enoki and king oyster in Dong Nai province using Japanese technology and harvesting robots.

name: Mushroom World
note: Thailand. Phuket farm growing oyster, straw, shiitake and lingzhi across 17,000 square feet, 100 to 200 tons a year.

name: Earthling Mushroom Farm
note: Thailand. Urban warehouse farm in Bangkok growing gourmet mushrooms for restaurants and open to visitors.

name: Agro Dutch Industries
note: India. Export oriented white button grower and canner at Lalru, Punjab, with its own can plant and 6 MW cogeneration. Entered insolvency on a State Bank of India application in November 2019, after a reported loss of 92 crore rupees in the 2011 financial year.

name: Denny Mushrooms
note: South Africa. The country's largest grower, supplying roughly half of national consumption. Libstar sold the fresh mushroom business with effect from December 2025, keeping and licensing the brand, and expected a pre tax loss on the disposal.

name: Pilze-Nagy
note: Hungary. Oyster mushroom grower near Kecskemet producing almost a million kilograms a year.

name: Monaghan Mushrooms
note: Ireland. Vertically integrated grower and substrate producer with about 3,500 staff and operations in Canada, the United Kingdom, Benelux and Germany.

name: Smallhold
note: United States. Filed for Chapter 11 in February 2024 and emerged in September 2024, closing its own farms in Texas, New York and California. Now sources from independent partner farms instead of growing.

name: Mykogen Polska
note: Poland. Leading substrate producer in central and eastern Europe at more than 150,000 tons a year. Acquired by Greenyard in June 2017 for about 93 million euros.

name: Walkro International
note: Netherlands. One of the largest substrate producers in the world at about 8,500 tons a week across Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany. Monaghan Mushrooms became sole shareholder in December 2018.

name: CNC Grondstoffen
note: Netherlands. Mushroom compost, casing soil, spawnable substrate and specialty blocks for shiitake, king oyster and almond mushroom. Private equity backed and acquiring, most recently Kompostpal in Poland in September 2025.

name: Christiaens Group
note: Netherlands. Turnkey builder of mushroom farms, composting yards and mycelium farms, including bunkers, tunnels, shelving, drawer systems and picking robots.

name: Mush Comb
note: Netherlands. Builds cultivation machinery, climate systems and picking lorries for growers in more than 50 countries.

name: Limbraco
note: Netherlands. Supplies mycelium harvesters, air handling, shelving and control computers, and converts Dutch style mushroom farms.

name: Amycel
note: United States. Produces mushroom spawn and supplements for commercial growers worldwide, with strain development and disease testing. Part of Monterey Mushrooms.

name: Groundwork BioAg
note: Israel. Mycorrhizal crop inoculants sold as Rootella for field and specialty crops and Dynomyco for cannabis. Raised 11 million dollars in 2021.

name: Mycorrhizal Applications
note: United States. Oregon producer of mycorrhizal inoculum under the MycoApply brand. Acquired by Valent BioSciences, part of Sumitomo Chemical, in March 2015.

name: Lallemand Plant Care
note: Mycorrhizal inoculants based on Rhizophagus irregularis and a biofungicide based on the mycoparasite Coniothyrium minitans.

name: Varsha Bioscience and Technology
note: India. Hyderabad maker of Trichoderma viride biofungicide, mycorrhizal biofertilizer and Beauveria, Metarhizium and Verticillium bioinsecticides.

name: T. Stanes and Company
note: India. Coimbatore maker of a Paecilomyces lilacinus biological nematicide registered with the national pesticide board, among other bio products.

name: Ballagro Agro Tecnologia
note: Brazil. Bioinput maker at Bom Jesus dos Perdoes registering Beauveria bassiana and Metarhizium anisopliae products. Reported revenue of about 200 million reais and says it is not seeking investment or a sale.

name: ABS Agrosoluciones
note: Colombia. Registered producer of Trichoderma, Beauveria and Metarhizium biologicals plus Glomus, Acaulospora and Gigaspora mycorrhizal inoculum, per the national agricultural institute register.

name: Bioquirama
note: Colombia. Registered producer of two Trichoderma species, Beauveria, Metarhizium and five genera of mycorrhizal fungi.

name: Invesa
note: Colombia. Registered producer of Trichoderma and Beauveria biologicals plus Glomus, Funneliformis, Rhizophagus and Diversispora mycorrhizal inoculum.

name: Agrimm Technologies
note: New Zealand. Trichoderma based crop protection and soil health, with more than four decades in the field. Partnered for Australia and New Zealand distribution in March 2026.

name: Biotelliga
note: New Zealand. Bioinsecticide from a fungus living inside grass plants plus a sprayable biofungicide. New Zealand regulators approved Corteva taking the remaining 80 percent on 27 May 2026.

name: Loam Bio
note: Australia. CarbonBuilder, a seed coating carrying a fungal inoculum intended to raise soil carbon as crops germinate. Raised about 73 million dollars in 2023. In October 2026 it cleared USDA permitting to expand use of its fungal seed coating to more US states.

name: Funga
note: Carbon removal company restoring belowground fungal communities in forests to speed tree growth and carbon capture. Raised 4 million dollars in seed funding in 2023.

name: Mycocycle
note: United States. Uses cultivated fungi to break down construction and demolition waste into feedstock for building materials. Raised 7.3 million dollars in total by 2024.

name: Angel Yeast
note: China. Asia's largest yeast producer. Its animal nutrition line sells yeast cell walls, hydrolysate and inactive yeast as feed ingredients.

name: Formo
note: Germany. Animal free cheese made from protein produced by koji fungus fermentation. In October 2026 Formo and Those Vegan Cowboys each received an FDA no questions letter for an animal free casein made by precision fermentation, under a notice the two filed together in December 2025. The source does not name the production organism.

name: MycoLutions
note: Germany. Grows mycelium through straw into the Woge acoustic panel, with fire safe and insulation versions in development. A second pilot plant has run since September 2025.

name: Myconom
note: Grows mycelium on farm and textile waste into acoustic and insulation panels for interiors. Headquarters country not stated in the source opened.

name: Anomalia Studio
note: India. Mumbai studio growing mycelium blocks from crop waste into furniture, partitions and an upholstery textile. Shown at the 2025 Venice Biennale. Partners with Mycotech Lab in Indonesia.

name: Redhouse Architecture
note: United States. Cleveland architecture practice that grows mycelium from demolition and crop waste and is developing a portable biocycler. The practice behind MycoHAB in Namibia.

name: Sapro-Tech
note: New Zealand. Auckland company growing mycelium into leather like textiles, partnered with four New Zealand fashion labels. Coverage and funding records stop in July 2024.

name: Mycelia
note: Belgium. Family business producing mushroom spawn and keeping several hundred fungal strains for growers.

name: Nuvedo
note: India. Bengaluru startup selling home mushroom growing kits and mushroom wellness products.

name: Motif FoodWorks
note: United States. Made a cow myoglobin in the yeast Pichia pastoris to give plant based meat a meaty flavor and color. Spun out of Ginkgo Bioworks in 2019, raised 345 million dollars, and was reported closing in September 2024.

name: Perfect Day
note: United States. Makes a whey protein in the fungus Trichoderma reesei. Raised almost 900 million dollars. In April 2024 its Italian manufacturer Olon sued for 112 million dollars in unpaid bills, saying payments stopped in August 2023.

name: Remilk
note: Israel. Makes a whey protein in the yeast Komagataella phaffii. Raised a 120 million dollar Series B in 2022, then paused its plan for a very large plant in Denmark in February 2023 and moved to a contract manufacturer.

name: Imagindairy
note: Israel. Makes a whey protein in the mold Aspergillus oryzae, used in a dairy range sold by Strauss Group. Just over 30 million dollars raised by January 2024.

name: ChangingBio (Shanghai Changing Biotechnology)
note: China. Makes a whey protein in the yeast Kluyveromyces lactis for milk, yogurt and baked goods. FDA response letter signed September 2025. Raised a 140 million yuan Series A in 2022.

name: All G
note: Australia. Makes bovine lactoferrin, a high value milk protein, in the yeast Komagataella phaffii. Raised 10 million Australian dollars in January 2026, 3 million of it from Agronomics, and has self affirmed GRAS status in the United States.

name: TurtleTree
note: Founded in Singapore. Makes bovine lactoferrin in the yeast Komagataella phaffii. FDA response letter signed May 2025. Moved its global headquarters to Ede in the Netherlands in October 2026 and handed women's health research on its lactoferrin to NIZO.

name: Eden Brew
note: Australia. Makes beta casein in the yeast Komagataella phaffii and has applied for food approval in Australia and New Zealand, with public comment closing in August 2026. Raised a 24.4 million Australian dollar Series A in 2023.

name: Vivici
note: Netherlands. Makes a whey protein in the yeast Komagataella phaffii, backed by Fonterra and dsm-firmenich. Raised a 32.5 million euro Series A in February 2025.

name: Verley (formerly Bon Vivant)
note: France. Makes a whey protein in the mold Aspergillus oryzae. FDA response letter signed September 2025. Raised a 38 million dollar Series A in February 2026.

name: Onego Bio
note: Finland and United States. Makes ovalbumin, the main egg white protein, in the fungus Trichoderma reesei, sold as Bioalbumen. About 65 million euros raised by July 2024.

name: The EVERY Company (formerly Clara Foods)
note: United States. Makes egg white proteins in the yeast Pichia pastoris for food and drink makers. A 55 million dollar Series D was reported in November 2025.

name: Helaina
note: United States. Makes a human lactoferrin, sold as effera, in the yeast Komagataella phaffii for supplements and child nutrition. Raised 83 million dollars in total by September 2024. Host named in a trade article rather than a filing.

name: Impossible Foods
note: United States. Makes soy leghemoglobin, the heme protein that gives its plant based meat a meaty flavor and color, in the yeast Komagataella phaffii. FDA response letter March 2025.

name: AB Enzymes
note: Germany. Darmstadt maker of food and feed enzymes produced in the fungus Trichoderma reesei. Part of a larger food group.

name: Shin Nihon Chemical
note: Japan. Maker of food and digestive enzymes, including an arabinase produced in the mold Aspergillus tubingensis.

name: Nanjing Bestzyme Bioengineering
note: China. Enzyme maker with a granted patent on glucoamylase produced in the mold Aspergillus niger.

name: Qingdao Vland Biotech Group
note: China. Feed and industrial enzyme group. It was an original co-holder of a patent on phytase made in the fungus Trichoderma reesei, transferred in 2022 to Qingdao Weilan Biological Group and Weifang KDN Biotech.

name: Oobli
note: United States. Makes the sweet protein brazzein in the yeast Komagataella phaffii, with FDA response letters from 2024 and 2025.

name: Amai Proteins
note: Israel. Makes Sweelin, a modified version of the sweet protein monellin, in the yeast Komagataella phaffii. FDA response letter February 2026.

name: NextFerm Technologies
note: Israel. Made the antioxidant pigment astaxanthin and a yeast protein using yeasts including Phaffia rhodozyma. Suspended operations in April 2025 except a joint venture in India, and its board sought a buyer.

name: Cabio Biotech
note: China. Wuhan maker of arachidonic acid oil for infant formula, produced in the fungus Mortierella alpina. Organism named in the company's own sponsored content.

name: Biocon
note: India. Large drug company whose human insulin is made in the yeast Pichia pastoris.

name: Jungbunzlauer
note: Switzerland, with plants in Austria and France. Major European citric acid maker using the mold Aspergillus niger.

name: Amyris
note: United States, with its plant in Barra Bonita, Brazil. Makes squalane, a stevia sweetener and other ingredients in baker's yeast. After its bankruptcy it took full ownership of the Brazilian plant from Ingredion in May 2025, and added a fourth production line in March 2026. In September 2025 it hired back Sunil Chandran, who had spent 17 years there, as chief technology officer.

name: Liberation Bioindustries (formerly Liberation Labs)
note: United States. Building a 600,000 liter precision fermentation plant in Richmond, Indiana. Its first customer, Vivici, makes whey protein in the yeast Komagataella phaffii. Construction is paused. In October 2026 its shareholder Agronomics said a four month review drew no acceptable offers for a sale or joint venture, and the company needs about 25 million dollars more, with full funding targeted for the first half of 2027.

name: Arsenale Bioyards
note: Italy. Builds "modular bio-reactor networks that scale out rather than up" and runs a pilot site in Pordenone. Works with microbes such as yeast. Raised $10 million in seed funding in February 2025.

name: Acies Bio
note: Slovenia. Develops and manufactures for clients, offering biomanufacturing services backed by two decades of in house research and development. Scales up engineered Aspergillus niger strains licensed from Ginkgo Bioworks. Largest tank 30,000 liters, with another due to start in late 2026.

name: Novonesis
note: Denmark. Formed in January 2024 when Novozymes and Chr. Hansen combined. Sells enzymes, cultures and other biosolutions across more than 30 industries, including food, agriculture, bioenergy and household care. About 10,000 staff and about 3.7 billion euros in annual revenue at formation.

name: IFF
note: United States. Acquired DuPont's Nutrition and Biosciences division in 2021, which carried the enzyme business that began with Genencor in Palo Alto. One of the largest industrial enzyme suppliers.

name: Scelta Mushrooms
note: Netherlands. Supplies mushroom based ingredients for blended meat and vegetarian products.

name: Fotortec
note: Chile. Grows mushrooms on food waste and turns them into flavorings, protein, feed and packaging, licensing the method to partners. No coverage found after August 2023.

name: Numinus Wellness
note: Canada. Psychedelic therapy company licensed by Health Canada in June 2020 to produce and extract psilocybin, with plans to grow mushrooms at its Nanaimo lab. Under a cease trade order from January 2025, five subsidiaries assigned into bankruptcy in March 2025, and shares delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange effective April 22 2026.

name: PsyBio Therapeutics
note: Developed biosynthetic production of psychedelic compounds, including 5-MeO-DMT. Trading on the TSX Venture Exchange suspended since December 2023, and moved to the board for inactive companies in March 2024.

name: Compass Pathways
note: United Kingdom. Developing COMP360, a synthetic psilocybin, and expects to finish its United States approval filing in late 2026.

name: KAAPA Biotech
note: Finland. Grows and extracts organic functional mushrooms such as chaga, reishi and lion's mane.

name: Mycrobez
note: Switzerland. Basel maker of a mycelium foam grown on organic waste, mainly for packaging. Still active in the Swiss company register in June 2026, but no news after 2024 and several officers are listed as resigned.

name: Mykko (Osmose Studio)
note: United Kingdom. Mycelium leather alternative. Built a prototype production line in 2022; no later company news found.

name: Zvnder
note: Germany. Berlin label making wallets and accessories from tinder fungus, founded 2017. No coverage found after 2019. Also on the 2019 Cabane map.

name: Mycelia Tech
note: Ukraine. Ivano-Frankivsk maker of mycelium leather grown on farm byproducts. Holds a 400,000 euro EU grant for a pilot line running from 2026 to 2029.

name: HAU Bio-Based Materials
note: Turkey. Mycelium packaging, building and consumer products from farm waste. Last coverage 2023.

name: Radial
note: Mexico. Guadalajara maker of mycelium packaging grown on corn husks and other farm waste. Last coverage March 2024.

name: MycoFutures North Atlantic
note: Canada. Mycelium leather alternative for fashion.

name: MycoBuoys
note: United States. Maine maker of aquaculture buoys grown from fungi and hemp, founded 2022. A 2025 grant report says the buoys still lack a working waterproof coating and work is shifting to rafts for wetland restoration.

name: S.Lab
note: Ukraine. Packaging from hemp and mycelium to replace plastic foam. Active as of April 2025.

name: Smush Materials
note: Italy. Compostable mycelium packaging grown on farm byproducts in Lombardy. Active as of October 2024.

name: Fungal Architectures (FUNGAR)
note: European Union research project on building materials grown from fungi, coordinated by the University of the West of England, Bristol. Ran from December 2019 to May 2023.

name: PuriFungi
note: Belgium. Brussels maker of mycelium ashtrays that break down cigarette butts, and kits for cleaning soil with fungi. Last dated news March 2024.

name: MycoFarming
note: Netherlands. Amsterdam maker of modular water filters that use mycelium to remove persistent pollutants, founded 2023.

name: Mycophyto
note: France. Mycorrhizal biostimulants and soil restoration. Raised 16 million euros in January 2026 to build its first factory.

name: INOQ
note: Mycorrhizal products for farming, horticulture, land restoration and tree planting, founded 2001.

name: Bee Vectoring Technologies
note: Delivers the fungal biofungicide Clonostachys rosea CR-7 to crops by bumblebee. In May 2024 its board began looking for a buyer or other options.

name: Agrauxine by Lesaffre
note: Microbial crop products from the Lesaffre group, including a Trichoderma atroviride product against nematodes and fungal disease launched in the United States in January 2025.

name: Bosque Foods
note: Germany and United States. Whole cut meat alternatives from mycelium grown by solid state fermentation. Its Berlin arm went insolvent in 2024 and was liquidated; Infinite Roots bought the company in May 2026.

name: Hut and Stiel
note: Austria. Vienna grower of oyster mushrooms on used coffee grounds. New shareholders and capital registered in January 2026.

name: Better Nature
note: United Kingdom. Tempeh products sold in UK supermarkets. Raised 1.1 million pounds in August 2025.

name: Fable Food Co
note: Australia. Sydney maker of shiitake based meat alternatives and a shiitake blend for mixing with beef.

name: Adamo Foods
note: United Kingdom. Whole cut steak alternative made from fermented mycelium. Won an EU grant in May 2026 for a three year scale up.

name: Esencia Foods
note: Spain, with a German arm. Whole cut seafood and meat alternatives from mycelium grown by solid state fermentation. EU funded project runs to May 2027.

name: MAASH
note: Belgium. LoCylia mycoprotein from a filamentous fungus grown in liquid tanks, for blended meat and pet food. Raised 12.15 million euros in 2026 to launch a demonstration plant at Carling-Saint-Avold, France.

name: Soma Tech
note: Ireland. Monaghan company making SomaMeal, a food ingredient from by-products fermented with fungi.

name: MycoSure
note: South Africa. High protein mycelium powder from four fungal strains, sold to food makers. Last dated news 2023.

name: Optimized Foods
note: United States, Davis. Cultivated caviar on an edible mycelium scaffold, and a mycelium based fat. In the 2025 BEAM Circular Accelerator cohort. Last dated news February 2025.

name: Oleo Sustainable Palm Oil Solutions
note: United States, Berkeley. Grows oil rich yeast on sugars from farm and forest waste to make substitutes for palm oil. In the 2025 BEAM Circular Accelerator cohort. A summer 2026 internship listing is the latest sign of activity.

name: Ruby Bio
note: United States, Oakland. Makes clean label emulsifiers and sugar alcohols by fermentation with naturally occurring yeast licensed from UC Davis, with an emulsifier launch planned for 2027. In the 2026 BEAM Circular Accelerator cohort.

name: Fermeate
note: United States, California. Sells light controlled gene switches that let fermentation makers turn production on and off in yeast and bacteria. Raised a 2 million dollar seed round in April 2026. In the 2026 BEAM Circular Accelerator cohort.

name: The Yeast Bay
note: United States. Isolates, banks and sells specialty yeast and bacteria cultures for homebrewers and craft brewers, founded by Nick Impellitteri from work begun in 2013. White Labs has propagated and packaged its cultures since 2014. Its site carries a 2026 copyright.

name: Traitomic
note: Denmark, Copenhagen. Spun out of the Carlsberg Group's research lab in January 2023. Builds large libraries of natural genetic variants in crops and microbes and screens them for useful traits without genetic modification. Microbial work so far is reported in bacteria; growAG lists fungi among its targets.

name: Hyfe
note: United States. San Francisco company that began with microbial flour, then made sugars from food processing wastewater, and by August 2026 was splitting food side streams into fibers, bioactives and sugars using water, pressure and heat. That report describes no fungal growing. Kilogram scale, 11 million dollars raised.

name: Innomy
note: Spain. Mycelium burgers, sausages and nuggets under the Funka brand. No news after a 2022 funding round.

name: Seaqure Labs
note: Sweden. Mycelium protein for fish feed grown on grain and brewery waste; plans to raise money in 2026.

name: Nourish Ingredients
note: Australia. Tastilux, an animal free fat made in the fungus Mortierella alpina.

name: Melt and Marble
note: Sweden. Fats made by engineered yeast for food and cosmetics; self affirmed as safe for use in the United States in March 2026.

name: Clean Food Group
note: United Kingdom. Palm oil replacement made by yeast. Bought a research site in Liverpool in September 2025.

name: NO Palm Ingredients
note: Netherlands. Palm oil replacement made from a wild yeast strain; demonstration production planned for late 2026.

name: AIO
note: Estonia. Tallinn maker of yeast made oils, starting with cosmetics. Completed a one tonne production run in 2025.

name: Biomific
note: Fungi powered industrial wastewater treatment.

name: MY-FI
note: European Union research project, coordinated by SQIM in Italy, developing a fabric from fungal fibres grown on textile industry waste. Ran from November 2020 to October 2024.

name: Mush Composites
note: Hong Kong, with material grown in Chiang Mai, Thailand. Wall and surface tiles grown from mycelium as compostable replacements for marble and fibreboard. Exhibiting in 2026.

name: GOB
note: Compostable earplugs made from mycelium foam, distributed through concert promoters. Covered in March 2026.

name: BioFab
note: New Zealand. Auckland maker of packaging and building panels from mycelium and farm waste using Ecovative's process, founded 2018. Latest coverage 2023.

name: MushLume Lighting
note: United States. Brooklyn studio of designer Danielle Trofe growing lampshades from hemp and mycelium. Latest coverage October 2024. Also on the 2019 Cabane map.

name: Maia Farms
note: Canada. Vancouver company that moved from mycelium meat alternatives to mycelium ingredients for health products. Raised 3.75 million Canadian dollars; reported January 2026.

name: yeastup
note: Switzerland. Lyss company turning spent brewer's yeast into protein and fibre ingredients. Opened an industrial plant in late 2025.

name: 21st.BIO
note: Denmark and United States. Supplies engineered Aspergillus oryzae production strains and process help to companies making proteins by fermentation.

name: done properly
note: Chile. Fermented food ingredients including a mycoprotein, a savoury flavour enhancer and probiotics, with products in shops by 2025.

name: Tempty Foods
note: Denmark. Technical University of Denmark spinout making mycelium foods for salads, bowls and sandwiches. Funding recorded through March 2026.

name: Moku Foods
note: Jerky made from king oyster mushrooms, with new flavours due in shops in 2025.

name: Pan's Mushroom Jerky
note: United States. Mushroom jerky reported in more than 3,500 stores. Also on the 2019 Cabane map.

name: Phillips Mushroom Farms
note: United States. Kennett Square, Pennsylvania; the largest US grower of specialty mushrooms, also making mushroom ingredients.

name: Giorgio Fresh Co.
note: United States. Blandon, Pennsylvania mushroom grower, named a mushroom growing company of the year in 2025.

name: To-Jo Mushrooms
note: United States. Avondale, Pennsylvania family grower and shipper of fresh and prepared mushrooms. Also on the 2019 Cabane map.

name: Mycionics
note: Canada. Robotic mushroom harvesting and crop scanning, launched at large scale in July 2025.

name: 4AG Robotics
note: Canada. Salmon Arm, British Columbia maker of robots that harvest, trim and pack mushrooms. Raised a 40 million Canadian dollar Series B in 2025.

name: Fungi Perfecti
note: United States. Olympia, Washington company of Paul Stamets, making Host Defense mushroom supplements from mycelium.

name: FreshCap Mushrooms
note: United States. Functional mushroom extracts and supplements; began as a gourmet farm in 2015, with investment from The Giorgi Companies. Also on the 2019 Cabane map.

name: Spacegoods
note: United Kingdom. Coffee and matcha powders and drinks with mushrooms and adaptogens, in more than 850 added UK retail points by July 2026.

name: MUD WTR
note: United States. Coffee substitute made from mushrooms and cacao, plus creamers. Also on the 2019 Cabane map.

name: Mushroom Compadres
note: Portugal. Grows and processes functional mushrooms into tinctures, coffee, cacao and capsules sold across Europe.

name: FUNGTN
note: United Kingdom. Maker of alcohol free beer brewed with shiitake, lion's mane and reishi. Latest coverage June 2023.

name: Aloha Medicinals
note: United States. Carson City, Nevada grower of medicinal mushrooms such as cordyceps and reishi, supplying more than 700 companies.

name: North American Mycological Association
note: Nonprofit society of mushroom clubs, forays and publications.

name: New York Mycological Society
note: Membership society running walks, a fungus festival and courses.

name: British Mycological Society
note: United Kingdom. Charity founded in 1896 that manages the Fungal Records Database of Britain and Ireland.

name: Kapoose Creek Bio
note: Canada. Collects wild fungi on Vancouver Island and uses AI to find medicines; lead compound KCB-100. 2.2 million dollar partnership with McMaster University in May 2024.

name: Functional Mushroom Council
note: North American nonprofit for growers, suppliers and brands, working on research and quality standards. Launched January 2026; founding members include Fungi Perfecti, M2 Ingredients, Monterey Mushrooms and Far West Fungi.

name: Musheez (Natural Chaga)
note: Estonia. White label and private label mushroom extracts, capsules and bulk ingredients, launching a food and drink ingredient range in November 2026.

name: London Nootropics
note: United Kingdom. Coffee blends with lion's mane, cordyceps and other herbs, backed on Dragons' Den.

name: Shroomi
note: United States. Santa Barbara maker of mushroom wellness shots sold at Whole Foods. Last coverage 2020.

name: Eternal (formerly Kernel Mycofoods)
note: Argentina. Neutral tasting protein ingredient made by fungal fermentation, using AI and cameras to improve approved strains. Founded 2019; current operations not confirmed.

name: Banken Champignons
note: Mushroom grower and processor working on robot harvesting with 4AG Robotics; reported demand above supply in March 2026.

name: Agro-Projects
note: Poland. Builds complete mushroom farms and supplies substrate and machinery. Became a sponsor of the German mushroom growers' association in August 2026.

name: Urban Farm-It
note: United Kingdom. Lion's mane mushroom farm supplying Sainsbury's, expanding through a joint venture with Oakland International in late 2025.

name: GTL Europe
note: Netherlands. Venlo engineering team building mushroom growing and composting facilities and harvest machines, partnered with Hoving Group.

name: Shogun Maitake
note: Canada. London, Ontario grower of black maitake mushrooms and supplements, established 2015.

name: Bewilder
note: Singapore. Design studio founded in 2020 with its own small mushroom farm, making its own cultures and mycelium furniture.

name: PLP Labs
note: United Kingdom. Research arm of PLP Architecture in London, growing mycelium building blocks and pillars in its own lab. Its pillars won an award at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show in 2025.

name: Kineco
note: Netherlands. Grows mycelium foam and panels from straw fibres and mushroom leather waste at its own mushroom farm. Material listed August 2025.

name: Joil Industries
note: South Korea. Busan firm leading research on mycelium leather for car interiors and consumer goods; prototypes to be tested with Hyundai Transys, announced August 2025.

name: Mykilio
note: Czech Republic. Brno firm growing mushroom leather, wall panels and insulation; part of the team behind the Samorost mycelium house shown in 2025.

name: Rebound
note: Denmark. Mycelium startup making an interior door with Det Levende Hus, plus acoustic wall and ceiling panels. Door prototype reported April 2026.

name: Klarenbeek and Dros
note: Netherlands. Studio that 3D prints mycelium. Built a mycelium facade with the builder Heijmans, reported August 2025.

name: Spore.nl
note: Grew the mycelium for the Growing Matter(s) pavilion with Henning Larsen at Milan Design Week, April 2025.

name: Pitri
note: Startup founded in 2024 growing fungal pigments to replace synthetic colorants, starting with beauty products.

name: Fabulous Fungi
note: Netherlands. Rotterdam startup growing fungi for textile dyes; partnered with the sportswear brand Iron Roots in 2023.

name: BioLab Studio
note: United States. California studio growing mycelium on 3D printed scaffolds tended by a robot arm. Reported December 2022.

name: AFJD
note: Studio of Joe Dahmen and Amber Frid-Jimenez using oyster mushroom mycelium for building materials, including a brick wall at the Museum of Vancouver.

name: MYCO-PAN
note: Finland. European Union project led by VTT to grow mycelium panels for inside and outside buildings. Runs September 2026 to February 2030.

name: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
note: Finland. Makes mycelium leather and foams by liquid fermentation and leads the MYCO-PAN project.

name: Korea Institute of Materials and Components Convergence
note: South Korea. Runs the test phase of Busan's mycelium leather program and is building a public testbed with mycelium growing, due by 2027.

name: Bio Base Europe Pilot Plant
note: Belgium. Ghent pilot plant that scaled up mycelium fibre fermentation for the MY-FI project, 2020 to 2024.

name: Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology
note: China. A synthetic biology lab there grew a living Cordyceps mycelium textile that repairs itself, published in July 2026.

name: Utrecht University
note: Netherlands. Mycelium material research; partner in MY-FI and FUNGAR and host of the MyBond fellowship on how mycelium binds wood waste.

name: University of the West of England
note: United Kingdom. Bristol lab growing mycelium to study it as electronics; led FUNGAR, which ended in May 2023.

name: Royal Danish Academy
note: Denmark. Its Biolab, set up in 2020, makes mycelium composites; FUNGAR partner.

name: University of Maribor
note: Slovenia. European Space Agency contract to develop a stronger mycelium composite for 3D printing, November 2023 to November 2026.

name: Hochschule Anhalt (InMyco)
note: Germany. Two research groups building a library of mycelium material samples and prototypes, funded July 2024 to December 2027.

name: BIBA Bremen (MycelCycle)
note: Germany. Leads a four year project with Goettingen on recyclable mycelium packaging, funded with 1.26 million euros by the Volkswagen Foundation.

name: Living Textiles Research Group
note: United Kingdom. Newcastle group growing mycelium on knitted fabric to make building structures; showed the Pupa installation in May 2025.

name: TU Berlin Applied and Molecular Microbiology
note: Germany. Partner in MycoColors, an art school project developing textile dyes from fungi, published 2025.

name: Champignon Brands (now Braxia Scientific)
note: Canada. Former psilocybin and mushroom company renamed Braxia Scientific, which runs depression clinics. Ontario issued a cease trade order in August 2024 for failing to file accounts; the exchange lists it as suspended.

name: Silo Wellness
note: United States. Oregon psilocybin company listed in Canada. In June 2025 it announced a change of business into defense finance as Born Defense, with a new chief executive in August 2025.

name: Cidara Therapeutics
note: United States. San Diego developer that began in antifungals; its lead drug by the time of sale was a flu preventive. Merck completed a 9.2 billion dollar purchase in January 2026.

name: Pulmocide
note: United Kingdom. London developer of opelconazole, an inhaled antifungal for lung aspergillosis. Stopped its Phase 3 trial in January 2026 after early data showed fewer good responses and more deaths.

name: Anacor Pharmaceuticals
note: United States. Developed the nail fungus drug tavaborole. Pfizer completed its purchase in June 2016.

name: MacroChem
note: United States. Developed EcoNail, a lacquer for nail fungus. Bought by Access Pharmaceuticals in February 2009.

name: Blueberry Therapeutics
note: United Kingdom. Alderley Park maker of skin treatments including antifungals for nail and foot fungus; its athlete's foot spray finished Phase 2.

name: Kathera Bioscience
note: United States. Develops broad spectrum antifungal drugs; won a federal award of up to 597,060 dollars in September 2023.

name: Prokaryotics
note: United States. Develops antibiotics and antifungals against drug resistant yeasts and molds; won a 2.875 million dollar NIH award in September 2023.

name: NovaBiotics
note: Developing Novamycin, an antifungal for drug resistant infections; won 1.8 million pounds from Innovate UK in February 2019.

name: Tryptamine Therapeutics
note: Australia. Develops psilocybin and intravenous psilocin drugs, listed on the ASX. Enrolled patients in a binge eating disorder trial in November 2025.

name: BLS Pharmaceuticals (formerly Bioxyne)
note: Australia. Licensed maker of cannabis, MDMA and psilocybin medicines through Breathe Life Sciences. Renamed in June 2026.

name: HYTN Innovations
note: Canada. Licensed to make psilocybin for clinical use and bought Prism Scientific Labs for mushroom growing methods; its 2025 news covers only cannabis exports.

name: Psygen
note: Canada. Calgary maker of psilocybin and other psychedelic drug ingredients for clinical and research clients, now mainly a contract manufacturer.

name: Shortwave Life Sciences
note: United Kingdom listed. Developing a psilocybin based drug for anorexia; its January 2026 results warned it needs more funding to keep going.

name: Apex Labs
note: Canada. Vancouver developer of APEX-90, a psilocybin capsule for depression in people with PTSD; Israel approved new trial sites in June 2025.

name: Revive Therapeutics
note: Canada. Toronto drug developer with a psilocybin program among others; extended a private placement in September 2025.

name: CB Therapeutics
note: United States. Carlsbad, California company making psilocybin, psilocin and other psychedelics by yeast fermentation. Has raised 11.62 million dollars.

name: Satya
note: United States. Oregon psilocybin manufacturer and service center; renewed its state manufacturing licence in June 2025 and has served over 1,000 clients.

name: Satori Farms PDX
note: United States. Woman owned Portland farm that received Oregon's first psilocybin manufacturing licence in March 2023.

name: Valor Minds
note: United States. Veteran led company approved in Colorado's first round of psilocybin business licences in February 2025, planning a small growing site in Englewood.

name: Entheogyn
note: United States. Colorado psilocybin startup planning to grow, make and give psilocybin therapy; growing and healing center licences pending as of May 2025.

name: Serenus Global
note: Canada. Calgary company licensed by Health Canada in August 2022 to produce and sell psilocybin; also makes coffee and edible mushroom products.

name: PurMinds NeuroPharma
note: Grows psilocybin mushrooms and develops a non hallucinogenic drug; latest news June 2024 on its first botanical psilocybin delivery.

name: NeonMind Biosciences
note: Canada. Oakville developer of psilocybin for obesity; last reported earnings February 2023, with market value shown near zero.

name: Rose Hill
note: Jamaica. Calls itself the largest legal producer of psilocybin mushrooms and made the first legal export from Jamaica to Canada; owns One Retreats.

name: Anahit Therapeutics
note: Jamaica. Canadian owned startup building farms to grow mushrooms and extract psilocybin; New Wave Holdings owned 75 percent by September 2020.

name: Mycolove Farm
note: United States. Colorado farm founded in 2021 growing and extracting functional mushrooms such as lion's mane and reishi.

name: Psyched Wellness
note: Canada. Toronto maker of supplements from the Amanita muscaria mushroom; filed an FDA new ingredient notice in July 2025 and sold out its first production run in January 2026.

name: Fantastic Fungi
note: Mushroom supplement brand named after the documentary, selling lion's mane and reishi capsules and elixirs; launched in every Sprouts store in July 2026.

name: Purely Mushroom
note: United States. Atlanta supplement brand; launched three mushroom gummies in March 2026.

name: Monterey Nutra

note: UK. British arm of a Dutch-owned mushroom grower went into administration after significant losses and a summer fire at its Thakeham headquarters. Article date not shown.

name: Walsh Mushrooms
note: Ireland. Gorey-based supplier of over 500 tonnes of fresh mushrooms a week to the UK. March 2025: planned a 10 million pound robotic growing site near Evesham.

name: Van Namen Group
note: Netherlands. Velddriel grower of white and chestnut mushrooms, about 160 tons a week, with a new growing and packing site. October 2026: weak season after summer heat.

name: MushVision
note: AI app from an India-based team that counts and measures mushrooms on growing beds and forecasts growth. October 2026: seeking Dutch growers to test it.

name: Nam
note: Portugal. Start-up growing mushrooms on used coffee grounds with Delta Cafes. September 2026: investing 1 million euros in an Odivelas factory for 150 tonnes a year.

name: IGS Agro
note: Russia. Largest mushroom producer in Tatarstan, growing white and royal mushrooms from its own compost. Produced about 3,900 tons in 2023.

name: ECO GLADE LLP
note: Kazakhstan. Built the country's largest mushroom complex in North Kazakhstan, up to 2,400 tonnes a year. December 2025: planning a compost plant and expansion.

name: RibbStyle
note: Maker of coatings for mushroom farms, for example rust protection on growing room doors. The site's dates appear to be display dates, so none is reliable.

name: Tiantianxiang Food Co., Ltd
note: China. Shanxi company founded 2013 that grows, processes and trades mushrooms. May 2019: exported 36 tons of canned shiitake to Malaysia.

name: Guizhou Wantai Modern Agricultural Food Co
note: China. Guiyang producer of dried mushrooms with six production lines. July 2020: first Guiyang mushroom export, 25,000 kg to Thailand.

name: Bac Au High-Tech Food JSC
note: Vietnam. Runs an automated mushroom plant in Buon Ma Thuot built in 2023, producing 1,800 tons a year of enoki and other specialty mushrooms. Reported November 2025.

name: Vinamit
note: Vietnam. Develops processed and medicinal mushroom products; its dried shiitake chips are among its best sellers. Reported November 2025.

name: Tu Thao Mushroom Export Process Company
note: Vietnam. Soc Trang mushroom export processor that filled only about a third of its export orders for lack of supply. Latest page is from 2012.

name: Shri Shyam Mushroom Farm
note: India. Button mushroom farm in South West Delhi producing about 40,000 kg a year in cold rooms, sold at Azadpur Mandi.

name: Costa Group (Costa Mushrooms, MushBoom)
note: Australia. Grower and packer of mushrooms with farms in South Australia, Victoria and Western Australia; sells under MushBoom. April 2026: added 40 tons a week of capacity.

name: Red Valley Farms
note: Australia. Banana grower that opened a 9,600 square meter facility growing shiitake, oyster and shimeji. May 2026: its largest investment to date.

name: TUJAY Mushrooms
note: Kenya. Solar-powered, climate-controlled mushroom farm in Kilifi selling to tourist hotels. No dated page found.

name: Bannie-El Farm
note: Kenya. Button mushroom farm in Kiambu County started by seven graduates, selling to Nairobi restaurants and supermarkets. Latest page is from 2018.

name: Sapphire Organic Farm
note: Kenya. Joska, Machakos County farm growing oyster mushrooms and vegetables, selling to Nairobi hotels and restaurants. Article undated.

name: GEPC (Groupement Europeen des Producteurs de Champignons)
note: European mushroom growers group. Its chair was at the Dutch Mushroom Days fair, and September 2026 news says it will submit a second EU promotion campaign.

name: Mushrooms Canada
note: Canada. Voluntary non-profit founded 1955 whose members are growers, processors, spawn makers, suppliers and scientists. Latest page is from 2023.

name: Mushroom Growers Association of Kenya
note: Kenya. Growers association with about 100 members in 23 counties that supplies supermarkets and hotels. Latest page is from 2019.

name: Fungipor
note: Argentina. Salta company growing mycelium on bean straw and other farm waste into compostable packaging that replaces plastic and polystyrene. Grew out of Hongos del Valle around 2019; clients include a Chandon wine pack.

name: Hongos del Valle
note: Argentina. Edible mushroom farm in Cerrillos, Salta, founded in 2001 by biologist Ayelen Malgraf. Sells oyster mushrooms to restaurants, hotels and shops in Salta. Parent of the packaging venture Fungipor.

name: Sporonex
note: Latvia. Startup making sound absorbing panels for studios from mycelium and circular waste materials. Featured on Monocle radio in September 2025.

name: Myko
note: Spain. Valencia startup from two Polytechnic University of Valencia graduates making modular wall panels from farm waste grown with mycelium. Took second place in the Spanish Climate Launchpad final in June 2025.

name: Muush
note: Brazil. Ponta Grossa company growing a leather alternative from mycelium on sawdust, straw and coffee grounds. Left its university incubator in October 2023; not yet sold commercially as of December 2024. Likely sister company of Mush.

name: RongoDesign
note: Romania. Grows mycelium on wheat straw, corn stalks and sawdust into insulation and wall panels, furniture and packaging. Founded 2021 by Gabriel Barta; had first paying customers in 2023. Latest coverage August 2023.

name: Mylium
note: Netherlands. Wageningen startup founded in 2018 by Iris Houthoff, growing textiles from mycelium as an alternative to leather, silk and wool. Planned a pilot factory for late 2021. Latest dated coverage March 2023.

name: Mycosuisse
note: Switzerland. Emmenbrucke company near Lucerne growing building panels and bricks from oyster mushroom mycelium and wood chips. Floor tiles were tested at the Stapferhaus in Lenzburg in 2022.

name: S-BIOTICA
note: Spain. Barcelona biodesign and research studio co-founded by Jessica Dias, making prototypes from mycelium and other living materials. Ran a study on mycelium surfboards from 2022 to 2023.

name: BioNate
note: India. Agra company at prototype stage making packaging from mycelium. Set up in 2023 and incubated at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University.

name: Mushroom-X
note: Hong Kong. Social enterprise started in March 2018 by Prof. Kwan Hoi Shan's team at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, making mycelium materials for packaging and insulation from coffee grounds and wood chips.

name: Bionatur-All
note: Argentina. Small Cosquin, Cordoba venture making Mushpack, a compostable packaging grown from mycelium on hay or sawdust. A mushroom leather was in research. Latest coverage 2022.

name: REDDO Biodesign
note: Chile. Valparaiso startup growing mycelium on recycled paper and sawdust into packaging and interior wall coverings, meant to replace polystyrene. Latest coverage August 2022.

name: Mush Bio
note: Interior design venture making wall panels and coverings from industrial waste and mycelium. Covered by an Ecuador outlet in June 2022, but the page does not state its country.

name: Glen Biotech
note: Spain. University of Alicante spin-off selling Beauveria bassiana 203, a fungus against the red palm weevil. Bought by Symborg, announced January 2022 and completed March 2022. Corteva agreed to buy Symborg in September 2022.

name: MultiBioCrop (University of Thessaly)
note: Greece. University research team building a plant protection and crop feeding product based on beneficial fungi. Named a Top 5 Innovator in the Future is Fungi Award 2026, chosen from 126 teams.

name: MyPilz
note: Austria. Vienna company using fungi to break down or lock up soil pollutants, offering species selection, lab tests and field support. Looking for Horizon Europe zero pollution project partners in March 2026.

name: Meet Future
note: Estonia. Developing whole cut chicken and fish alternatives from mycoprotein. Opened a 400,000 euro seed round in September 2022 and won a plant based startup contest that October. No later news found.

name: Niskus Biotec
note: Ireland. Grows mycelium in liquid fermentation on brewery and distillery spent grains to make protein and enzymes for food and feed. Running pilots with breweries and distilleries in late 2025.

name: Mycelium Technologies
note: France. Saclay startup founded in April 2022 that grows mycelium on discarded pulses into mynion, a meat-like food for professional buyers. Won Best Culinary Innovation at Sirha 2025; launch planned for late 2026.

name: Mycrocell
note: Singapore. Food startup growing mushroom mycelium as a protein for processed foods and testing mycelium extracts for skincare. Latest coverage October 2022.

name: Puurfection
note: United Kingdom. Supplement company that grows organic lion's mane mushrooms and sells mushroom supplements and a lion's mane coffee made with Baytown Coffee in May 2025. Sources differ on Norfolk or Yorkshire.

name: Lykaia
note: Germany. Aichtal brand from founder Jana Baltscheit adding functional mushrooms to coffee and superfood products. Appeared on the TV show Die Hohle der Lowen. Latest coverage September 2024.

name: MushUp
note: Canada. Montreal maker of coffee blended with reishi, lion's mane and chaga, founded in 2019 and sold online and in health food stores.

name: Emberk
note: Canada. Calgary mushroom coffee and latte brand led by women, using six mushrooms including lion's mane, reishi and chaga. Ships across Canada and to the United States.

name: Dougall Tea
note: Canada. Bridgewater, Nova Scotia maker of mushroom teas and coffees, begun in 2023 by Shaun MacDougall with family chaga blends.

name: Peak State Coffee
note: United States. Boulder coffee company founded in 2020 by Danny Walsh, selling organic beans infused with reishi, lion's mane, cordyceps and chaga. Named to a fast growth list in a paid July 2026 release.

name: Sun and Silo
note: United States. Littleton, Colorado functional mushroom brand owned by founder Kim Koehler, selling mushroom gummies and a ten-mushroom capsule. Latest coverage September 2022.

name: The Fungamental Co.
note: India. Calls itself India's first vertically integrated mushroom lab, growing, extracting and bottling lion's mane, cordyceps and reishi tinctures. Sources differ on Bangalore or Goa.

name: Popadelics
note: United States. New York brand from Fun-Gal Snacks making crunchy shiitake mushroom chips. Launched April 2022 and expanded to about 205 Whole Foods stores in 2024.

name: Eat the Change
note: United States. Seth Goldman and Spike Mendelsohn brand that launched smoked mushroom jerky in 2021. A 2023 interview suggests the jerky was dropped, and the brand now pushes teas.

name: Ichimasa Kamaboko
note: Japan. Niigata fish paste maker listed in Tokyo that also runs a maitake business from its own growing centres. Worked with Nanyang Technological University on an oyster mushroom mycelium protein study in 2026.

name: Maine Cap N Stem
note: United States. Maine supplier of spawn, colonized sawdust blocks and substrate to farms in the US and Canada. Bought a 75,600 square foot Lewiston building in 2022; joined the Functional Mushroom Council in May 2026.

name: Mushroom Supply Services
note: United States. Kennett Square, Pennsylvania distributor of grower supplies and US partner of RibbStyle since 2024.

name: Kekkila-BVB
note: Netherlands, Finland, Sweden and Estonia. Growing media group whose Dutch arm, BVB Substrates, makes casing soil for mushroom farms. Its BIOSCHAMP trials found peat could be cut, not replaced.

name: Fungi Fresh Farms
note: United States. Grimes, Iowa gourmet mushroom farm in a converted shipping container, harvesting 50 to 100 pounds a week for markets and restaurants in 2022.

name: The Danish Morel Project
note: Denmark. Twin biologists Jacob and Karsten Kirk grow black morels indoors in climate chambers all year, using a patented method. They say commercial production needs automation first.

name: La Caverne
note: France. Organic farm run by Cycloponics in an underground car park in northern Paris, growing oyster mushrooms, shiitake and endives. Public visit set for October 2026.

name: La Boite a Champignons
note: France. Grows oyster mushrooms on used coffee grounds at Saint-Nom-la-Breteche and sells home kits. Taken over by Kroptek in 2021. Reports 78,000 kg of mushrooms grown.

name: Yorkshire Mushroom Emporium
note: United Kingdom. Leeds urban farm growing gourmet mushrooms for local restaurants and shops, also selling grow kits. Received 50,000 pounds of start up loans in 2025.

name: Mycycling Mushrooms
note: United Kingdom. Cockfield, Teesdale grower run by Jordan Bain, growing lion's mane and oyster mushrooms on leftover sawdust and selling grow kits. Latest coverage July 2022.

name: GroCycle
note: United Kingdom. Devon social enterprise founded by Adam Sayner and Eric Jong, teaching mushroom farming since 2009 through an online course with over 3,000 members, and selling home grow kits.

name: Sporadic Fungi
note: United Kingdom. Small farm at Langham near Colchester run by Harry Wilton and Georgia Wills, growing colourful oyster mushrooms and lion's mane for farm shops and restaurants.

name: Coonfresh
note: India. Alappuzha, Kerala oyster mushroom farm with over 6,000 beds, run by Shije Varghese and TJ Thankachan. Has trained over 10,000 farmers.

name: Imperial Fungal Science Network
note: United Kingdom. Imperial College London network for mycologists covering advocacy, communication and training of future fungal research leaders. Ran a public stand at the Great Exhibition Road Festival in June 2026.

name: Magan Centre of Applied Mycology
note: United Kingdom. Cranfield University centre for applied fungal research toward net zero and biotechnology. Officially opened on 3 October 2025.

name: Australian Mushroom Growers Association
note: Australia. Main industry body for mushroom growers. In 2023 it said 47 growers produce the common varieties in an industry worth over 460 million dollars a year.

name: Funga Conservacion
note: Costa Rica. Fungi conservation group that runs the Ruta Micologica fungi tourism route with Oropopo Experience. Co-director is Luis Francisco Ledezma. Route ran again in May 2025.

name: Museo del Hongo
note: Chile. Travelling pop-up museum mixing art and science about fungi, founded in 2016 by Juan Ferrer. Shown at Ars Electronica and Berlin Science Week; events in New York in May 2024.
